chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Ali (peace be upon him), when two men came to him with witnesses, their justice being equal and their number equal, would draw lots between them to see upon which of them the oath would fall. He said: And he would say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, whichever of them had the right, grant it to him.' Then he would assign the right to the one to whom the lot fell, when he swore the oath.

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ السَّبْعِ: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve disputes when witnesses for both sides were equal in number and justice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the judicial mechanism of *Yamin* (oath) employed by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) when two parties presented equal evidence, reflecting the Shia principle of *Hajjiyyah* (presumption of validity) in the absence of definitive proof. By drawing lots to select the oath-taker, the Imam ensured impartiality, invoking divine assistance to guide the true claimant, a practice that underscores the spiritual dimension of legal adjudication in Shia jurisprudence. This method highlights the balance between procedural fairness and reliance on God's will in resolving ambiguous disputes.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever they came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with two men with witnesses equal in being just and in number, he<sup>asws</sup> would draw a lot upon whichever the oath would come to be. And he<sup>asws</sup> would be saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the seven skies! For whomever the right was, so Make it to be for him’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> would make the right to be for the one to whom it (the lot) came to be, when he swore an oath’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’ Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, whenever two people came before him with just witnesses in equal numbers, would cast a raffle about who must take the oath.’

He (the Imam) said that he (the Imam) would say, ‘O Lord of the seven heavens, whoever is right then make it available for him’ and he would decide in favor of the one whose raffle came out for taking the oath; if he took the oath.’”
